subject.title: [Feature Request]: Session snapshots — save and load context checkpoints (/session save|load)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class named session snapshots now, and what should the first supported scope be: arbitrary save/list/load, archive restore, checkpoint branch/restore, prompt-cache-aware fork, or a narrower subset?
rationale: The source shows multiple adjacent primitives but no single product contract for named snapshots, and choosing restore, branch, retention, archive-import, and prompt-cache semantics is a maintainer product/API decision.

options.title: Design core snapshot API first
options.body: Create a maintainer-owned design that unifies named checkpoints, restore/branch behavior, archive import, privacy rules, and protocol/command surfaces before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to resume/archive restore
options.body: Let focused `/resume` or read-only archive recovery work land first while keeping named checkpoints and deterministic snapshot diff tracked separately.

options.title: Defer named snapshots
options.body: Keep compaction checkpoints, export commands, and subagent fork as separate primitives until maintainers choose a broader snapshot direction.

recommendation.title: Design core snapshot API first
recommendation.body: Create a maintainer-owned design that unifies named checkpoints, restore/branch behavior, archive import, privacy rules, and protocol/command surfaces before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided prior review context on this issue and recently worked on adjacent session UI/protocol surfaces.
